title: Thresholds and expectation thresholds
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's proof (2026) of the second Kahn-Kalai conjecture: for every graph H with h >= 1 edges and at most n vertices, the threshold for G(n,p) to contain a copy of H is at most 2048 e^50 p_E(n,H)(1 + log_2 h), where p_E(n,H) is the least p at which every subgraph of H has at least 1/2 expected copies. The first lesson develops random subsets, increasing families, covers, expectation thresholds and copy counts, and shows with perfect matchings that a logarithmic factor is necessary. The second proves the planted resampling step for spread families; the third proves the tree covering theorem, with the spread lemma as the one-level case; the fourth builds the tree of conditional extensions of H and proves the theorem.
